perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. We have a cordial but sometimes strained professional relationship because we disagree on sales and marketing strategies.
- In a meeting room, I prepared data and charts supporting traditional sales techniques. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed core sales could benefit more from traditional methods, and I presented data from our last five campaigns.
- I heard Katherine say the market is evolving, that digital outreach has potential, and ask how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement. I replied that I was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing, but felt proven methods were being sidelined without proper consideration. Katherine said she understood and suggested analyzing data together to integrate both approaches.
- Later, Katherine shared recent digital-campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. I asked her to explain how those strategies are developed. She said it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making process. I admitted I had doubts but seeing the outcomes made me want to understand digital more. She said she was glad I was open to exploring it and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting to integrate traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed and said we should schedule a time to brainstorm and outline next steps. I said I was hopeful that leveraging both our expertise could create something impactful, and I appreciated her willingness to collaborate. She said she looked forward to it and to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After the joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas. I showed it to Katherine. She reviewed it, said it looked comprehensive and well thought out, and that my hard work showed. I said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors and that I wanted to nail the presentation. She said with that level of preparation she was confident and suggested fine-tuning areas that needed it.
- After our presentation and the implementation of the new strategy, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our successful collaboration. I thanked Katherine, saying I had learned much from her. She said it had been a pleasure seeing the project come to fruition and that my openness to new ideas made it a successful partnership. I proposed setting up regular strategy sessions. She agreed, saying they would keep us on top of our game and market trends.
